capabilities.purpose: Execute the bounded owner-attached curved polyline from hand to tip; collision checks every segment, while Projectile.Center is the terminal point. Lash progress follows the owner's current itemAnimation/itemAnimationMax; the projectile remains active only while that animation is positive, including when an activation delay ends. A baked/reused PNG draws once at that tip, not along the curve. runtime_geometry draws the exact collision curve; a separately authored VFX texturedPath source=whip can accompany a baked tip. A channel_beam controller takes collision/geometry precedence. No automatic sprite stretching or representation selection.

Move the body center from owner center + aimed axis * (18px + triangular range displacement), extending then retracting during the cycle. The axis follows the live owner cursor (bounded synced aim for remote owners) every AI update, rotating both body and hitbox; not a fixed initial launch axis. spawn.aim controls launch only, not this ongoing aim. This is not hand-attached: no native arm control, grip consumption or PNG stretching. It remains an independent legal movement choice.

Attach this explicit body's pose and collision center to the native front hand. Initial aim keeps the spawn axis; cursor aim follows synced live owner aim. No damage, lifecycle, visibility, asset or item-use choice is inserted. Collision center = native hand + aimed axis * hitboxOffsetPx, independent of PNG metadata; the existing axis-aligned rectangle is not pixel-matched blade collision. none-to-full stretch moves the hand only 6px; hitboxOffsetPx is a fixed center offset, not thrust reach or an extra sprite shift. Compare source use/collision geometry and resulting hand-to-damage coverage before deliberately choosing a short jab; sprite length alone adds no reach.
